findings.claim: The banned component-code pattern "Component 2" (matching the house validator's `Component \d` drift check, which rejects the whole unit on publish) appears six times: L1 content_html n19 "(Component 2, Section B Part 1)"; L6 content_html n20 "(Component 2, Section B Part 1)"; L7 description "Edexcel Component 2 Section B Part 1" (also makes the description 103 characters, over the 100-char validator limit); L7 content_html n2 "(Component 2, Section B Part 1)"; L7 knowledge_checks[0].q "Edexcel Component 2 Section B Part 1 comparison question"; L7 flashcard_questions[0].q "Edexcel Component 2 Section B Part 1 comparison worth".
findings.truth: The house style bans board component/paper codes; say "the Edexcel poetry comparison" / "this section" instead. All facts in these sentences (20 marks, AO2 15 + AO3 5, named poem printed) are correct per the spec — only the banned code wording needs to change.
findings.evidence: scripts/api_build/driver.py DRIFT_PATTERNS: `(r"Component \d", "component code")`; CHECK_PROMPT.md banned-strings list ("Component 1" example, same category).

findings.claim: The banned pattern "AO code immediately followed by a full stop" appears three times in L8: knowledge_checks[2].q ends "...15 for AO2 and 5 for AO3."; flashcard_questions[2].a is literally "AO2."; flashcard_questions[3].a is literally "AO3.".
findings.truth: Per CHECK_PROMPT.md this exact pattern is rejected by the validator. Reworded to keep the AO code away from a trailing full stop, e.g. "...5 for AO3 (context)." and "AO2, covering language, form and structure."
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT.md: 'never write an AO code immediately followed by a full stop'.

findings.claim: The same short quotation from Carole Satyamurti's "War Photographer" is given two different exact wordings in this unit: L2 content_html n11 — “The reassurance of the frame”; L8 content_html (quotation bank) — “The reassurance of the viewfinder.”
findings.truth: Cannot confirm which (if either) is verbatim — web search was unavailable this session (budget exhausted) and WebFetch could not reach any source that prints Satyamurti's "War Photographer" (Poetry Archive lists her other poems but not this one; poemanalysis.com, Genius, BBC and all search engines were blocked or 403). Two defensible options: (a) the poem really does use "frame" and L8 is wrong, (b) it uses "viewfinder" and L2 is wrong, or (c) both words appear in different lines and each lesson is a legitimate partial quote — in which case they should still be reconciled so no line is presented as more definitive than the other.
findings.evidence: L2 raw n11; L8 raw n17 (quotation bank entry for War Photographer). Recommend Tom check the printed Edexcel anthology / a library copy of Satyamurti's collected poems and align both lessons to the confirmed wording.

findings.field: content_html / glossary_terms / flashcard_questions (also recurs in L6)
findings.claim: Owen's "Exposure" is quoted throughout as "merciless iced east winds that knive us" (L1 content n5, flashcard; L1 knowledge_checks fill-blank; L6 content n13/n17), used as the anthology's flagship half-rhyme example.
findings.truth: Two independent full-text sources fetched this session (Wikisource 'Exposure', and Project Gutenberg ebook 1034, Owen's 1920 'Poems') both give "knife us", not "knive us", character for character. I could not corroborate "knive" from any source despite repeated attempts (BBC, Poetry Foundation and search engines were all blocked). I have some prior recollection of "knive" being the commonly cited GCSE spelling (possibly a later scholarly-edition variant, e.g. Stallworthy's Complete Poems), so this is genuinely unresolved rather than a confident fix.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Exposure and https://www.gutenberg.org/files/1034/1034-h/1034-h.htm both render the line with "knife us". Recommend checking the actual printed Edexcel anthology text, since that is the version students are marked against.

findings.claim: Jane Weir's "Poppies" is described as "commissioned by the Poetry Archive in 2009" (L2 key-fact and flashcard; L8 flashcard "commissioned for Remembrance Day").
findings.truth: Could not confirm this attribution. The Poetry Archive's own page for Jane Weir makes no claim to having commissioned "Poppies" (it only notes the poem is GCSE-studied). My working knowledge suggests the more commonly cited origin is Carol Ann Duffy's 2009 Guardian-commissioned "Exit Wounds" sequence of conflict poems, not the Poetry Archive, but theguardian.com was blocked to WebFetch this session so I could not confirm that alternative either.
findings.evidence: https://www.poetryarchive.org/poet/jane-weir/ (no commissioning claim). Recommend a quick check of a reliable Weir biography or the anthology teacher notes before editing.

findings.claim: Across all 8 lessons, 24 of 31 practice questions are labelled "type": "20 marks — Poetry Comparison" but their own mark scheme only awards up to 7-8 or 10-12 (not 20), and the question itself analyses ONE poem, not a comparison (e.g. L1 'How does Tennyson use repetition and rhythm in The Charge of the Light Brigade...' is labelled 20 marks/Poetry Comparison but its band ladder tops out at 7-8 and never mentions a second poem). Only the questions with a genuine two-poem prompt carry a matching Top band (16-20) ladder.
findings.truth: The real Edexcel Section B Part 1 question is always a 20-mark, two-poem comparison (AO2 15 + AO3 5, no AO1) — there is no such thing as a stand-alone single-poem question on this paper. Labelling single-poem analysis practice as "20 marks — Poetry Comparison" misrepresents the exam's actual format and could mislead a student's revision (writing to 7-8 marks' worth of content when the real question needs a sustained two-poem 20-mark response). Two defensible fixes: (a) relabel these as e.g. "8 marks — Poetry Analysis" / "12 marks — Poetry Analysis" to match their own band ladder, or (b) rewrite the question stems to add a second poem and expand the band ladder to 16-20. (a) is far less disruptive; not applied because it is 24 separate items and a judgement call, not a single surgical text fix.
findings.evidence: grep of "Top band" ranges against "type" labels across raw/L01.txt-L08.txt: every lesson has 2-3 mismatched instances (Top band max 7-8 or 10-12) alongside 1 correctly-banded (16-20) genuine comparison question. Spec: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md — Component 2 Section B overview + AO weighting table (AO2 15 / AO3 5, comparison-only).

summary: 8 lessons checked against specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md and the confirmed 15-poem Conflict anthology list. Exam-structure claims (20 marks, AO2 15/AO3 5, no AO1, no SPaG, closed book, named poem printed) are correct throughout and the collection is never confused with AQA's Power and Conflict. All public-domain quotations checked against Wikisource/Gutenberg were verbatim-accurate except one contested word. The two release-blocking issues are banned validator strings (F1, F2, both FIX); the rest are quotation/attribution conflicts I could not resolve because web search and most reference sites were unavailable this session (F3-F5), plus one systemic practice-question mislabelling pattern spanning all 8 lessons (F6).
